# Overview

`acme-tool` (`package.json` name, version `0.3.0`) is a 4-file Node package. `npm i` installs a
single `bin` entry, `acme` → `src/cli/main.js` (`package.json` `bin`). There is no other declared
entrypoint (no `main`/`exports` field) and no build step (`type: module`, plain ESM, no
transpiler config found).

## Kind

Classification is ambiguous between `cli` and `service` (`reference/agent-map.json`,
`_run/classify.json`): the package ships a `bin` entrypoint (cli evidence) and imports `express`
(web-framework evidence). This document treats it as **cli-shaped with an unused web dependency**
— see `GAP` in [Components](#components) for why, and the interview question `kind-ambiguous`
recorded at the end of this review for the open decision.

## Components

Three components, folded from `src/*/` (`docs/architecture/fold-rules.json`, `reference/components.md`):

| component | files | what it is | evidenced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli` | 1 (`src/cli/main.js`) | the `bin` entrypoint; on load it calls `run()` then `serve(express)` unconditionally, at module top level | `src/cli/main.js` |
| `core` | 2 (`src/core/run.js`, `src/core/back.js`) | `run()` returns the literal `1` and does nothing else; `back.js` re-exports `web`'s `serve` under the name `back` | `src/core/run.js`, `src/core/back.js` |
| `web` | 1 (`src/web/server.js`) | exports `serve(app)`, which ignores `app` and calls `run()`; also reads `process.env.ACME_API_TOKEN` into a local that is never used again | `src/web/server.js` |

**GAP:** `web` is folded from a directory named `web` and imports `express`, which is why the kit
classified it `webui`/service evidence — but no route, middleware, or `app.listen` call exists
anywhere in the file. The component receives an Express `app` and discards it. Nothing in this
repository actually serves HTTP. Whether `web` is meant to grow into a real server or is dead
scaffolding is not determinable from the code — see interview question `kind-ambiguous`.

## Dependency graph (why each edge exists)

| from | to | why | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cli` | `core` | `main.js` calls `run()` directly on load | `src/cli/main.js:1` |
| `cli` | `web` | `main.js` calls `serve(express)` directly on load | `src/cli/main.js:1` |
| `core` | `web` | `src/core/back.js` imports `src/web/server.js` to re-export `serve` as `back` | `src/core/back.js:1` |
| `web` | `core` | `src/web/server.js` imports `src/core/run.js` to call `run()` inside `serve()` | `src/web/server.js:1` |

`core` → `web` and `web` → `core` together form a 2-component import cycle (`reference/components.md`,
`reference/drift.json`). It is caused by a single file, `src/core/back.js`, which is not imported by
anything else in `src/` (checked directly: no other file references `back`). **The cycle currently
has no consumer** — `back` is exported but nothing in the repository imports it. See
`risks.md` and interview question `import-cycle-core-web`.

Because `main.js` calls both `run()` (via `core`) and `serve()` (which itself calls `run()` again
via `web` → `core`), **`run()` executes twice on every CLI invocation** — once directly, once
indirectly through `serve()`. This is a direct reading of the four files, not an inference from a
runtime trace: there is no test or log output to confirm it, so it is recorded as read, not observed.

## Runtime shape

There is exactly one path through the code (see `scenarios/cli-invocation.md`): process start →
`run()` → `serve(express)` → `run()` again → process exit. No branching, no error handling, no
async work, no network listener actually opened. `run()` is `() => 1`: its return value is
discarded by both call sites.

## What this is not

- Not a web service in the sense the `express` dependency and `web` directory name suggest — see
  the `GAP` above.
- Not under test: `reference/tests-by-seam.md` reports 0 test files.
- Not deployed anywhere findable in the repo: see `deployment.md`.
